articles.title: Is “November Theory” Coming for Your Relationship? Here’s What to Know Before You Spiral
articles.summary: November theory says the end of the year can trigger relationship doubts, but a therapist explains how to reflect before making a breakup decision.
articles.body:
The holidays are famously known as cuffing season. But for those already in relationships, this season could mean something entirely different.

"November theory" is the idea that this time of the year brings about a lot of reflection. For some people, this looks like exes coming back into their lives or someone entirely new coming into the picture. But for couples, this theory may signify endings.

Warnings like this usually come tied to astrology, but this theory circulates every November. So what is it about the 11th month of the year that seems to signal a doomsday for relationships ?

"As the end of the year approaches, people begin considering the new year and what they want for themselves," therapist Jessica Steinman, LMFT , tells Cosmopolitan . "People start discussing New Year's resolutions and intentions, and they consider who they want to have as a part of that."

And sometimes after reflection—and seeing how unhelpful your boyfriend is at Thanksgiving—people decide that it's time to call it quits.

So will this November be a death sentence for your relationship? Or will you come out on the other end of "November theory" in a stronger connection?

Okay, there's no legitimate research behind November causing mass breakups. But there is a reason the trend exists.

"The new year brings the psychological concept of 'fresh start effect' as well as reflection over the past year," Steinman explains.

While some people are mentally revising their workout routines or making resolutions to read more, they're also taking stock of what in their life is working and what isn't. Sometimes, the latter is their relationship. If they notice that they spent a majority of the year feeling uninterested and unhappy in or exhausted by their relationship, they may begin to think about whether the connection is even worth it.

"They want things to feel better, be easier, and move forward in the new year," Steinman says.

Should I Break Up With My Partner This November?

Before you get swept up in November theory, Steinman suggests taking a beat to think about the relationship as a whole.

"They need to consider if the struggles and issues in the relationship have been an ongoing concern or if this is something that could be intensified due to the stress and bigger feelings around the holidays," she says.

Sometimes dealing with the stresses of buying gifts, being around your problematic uncle, and having to spend time in your childhood home can trigger a lot of negative emotions. The holidays aren't always joy and cheer for everyone. And these stressors may be lending themselves to feelings of annoyance.

"They need to focus on the unhealthy patterns of what is going on in the relationship, not specific feelings that might be happening in those end-of-year moments."

And while it's fun to take part in internet trends, you should have a conversation with your partner before you make a video of yourself crying on TikTok post-breakup saying, "November theory is 100 percent real."

If something is genuinely bothering you about your relationship, communicate that to your partner. You might learn that your feelings of discontent have a pretty easy solution. "Change can't happen between partners if it isn't communicated and looked at together," Steinman says.

How to Use "November Theory" to Your Advantage

November theory doesn't necessarily mean you need to call it quits with your partner. It can actually be a really great opportunity to do some admin on your relationship.

"Having healthy, open, and vulnerable conversations with a partner before the new year is a great way to start the new year together," Steinman says.

She explains that rather than making an impulsive and permanent decision to end the relationship, couples can think of the end of the year as an assessment period and think about how they can make meaningful changes in the new year instead of giving ultimatums and ending it.

But this is a conversation that's going to require some thought. Steinman warns against using broad statements like "I'm unhappy" or "I don't wan't to do this anymore." They're just not productive.

"A statement like 'I feel like we've been disconnected' or 'I feel like we're not on the same page and I'd like to get on the same page' could work a lot better," she says. "Having a reflection conversation together is a good way to start."

Any trend that encourages you to reflect on your life and relationship is a trend I can get behind. But the second you start making decisions about your relationship because the internet told you to, you're going about it all wrong—and may even lose a good thing while you're at it.

Slow down, and take the time to think about what you want—and don't feel like you're confined to making your decision within the month. There's plenty of time to think about your relationship in December, too.

articles.standfirst: Vítima ainda não foi identificada. Corpo foi retirado do canal e ficou sob os cuidados da segurança do distrito de irrigação até a chegada do IML.
articles.summary: Corpo encontrado em Petrolina: a vítima foi localizada em um canal de irrigação no Projeto Nilo Coelho e aguarda identificação oficial pelo IML.
articles.body:

O corpo de um homem foi encontrado na tarde desta quinta-feira (26) em um canal de irrigação do Projeto N-6, no Projeto Nilo Coelho, na zona rural de Petrolina , no Sertão de Pernambuco. O nome da vítima não foi identificado.

articles.title: Com Uenf e Uerj entre as pioneiras, primeira Lei de Cotas Raciais do Brasil completa 25 anos | G1
articles.standfirst: Legislação sancionada no RJ em 2001 transformou universidades fluminenses; especialistas destacam importância das bolsas de assistência para a permanência estudantil.
articles.summary: Legislação sancionada no RJ em 2001 transformou universidades fluminenses; especialistas destacam importância das bolsas de assistência para a permanência estudantil.
articles.body:
A primeira lei de cotas raciais do Brasil completa 25 anos neste mês de novembro. Criada de forma pioneira no estado do Rio de Janeiro, a política pública transformou o perfil do ensino superior brasileiro ao ampliar o acesso de estudantes negros às universidades públicas. No entanto, após duas décadas e meia, especialistas e alunos apontam que o principal desafio atual é consolidar as políticas de assistência para garantir não apenas o ingresso, mas a permanência e a conclusão da graduação.

Adicione o g1 como Fonte Preferida no Google

A história das ações afirmativas nas instituições públicas brasileiras começou oficialmente em 9 de novembro de 2001, com a sanção da Lei Estadual 3.708. A norma reservou 40% das vagas para candidatos autodeclarados pretos e pardos nas duas principais universidades estaduais fluminenses: a Universidade Estadual do Norte Fluminense (Uenf), em Campos dos Goytacazes , e a Universidade do Estado do Rio de Janeiro (Uerj), na capital.

Mais de uma década após a iniciativa do Rio de Janeiro, a medida ganhou escala nacional com a Lei Federal 12.711, de 2012, que estendeu a reserva de vagas para todas as universidades e institutos federais do país. Atualmente, nas universidades estaduais fluminenses, a política é regulamentada pela Lei 8.121, de 2018, que prorrogou o sistema por mais dez anos e incluiu estudantes oriundos de comunidades quilombolas.

Para Etiene Martins, pesquisadora das relações étnico-raciais da Universidade Federal do Rio de Janeiro (UFRJ), a legislação nasceu para corrigir distorções históricas nos processos seletivos tradicionais.

"É uma política pública de educação. Visa a inserção social de pessoas pobres, negras, indígenas, quilombolas e PCDs no ensino superior nas universidades públicas. Essa política pública é fundamental para diversificar o perfil de pessoas que podem dar continuidade aos seus estudos. Isso porque, mesmo no Brasil a educação sendo um direito básico, não tem vaga para todo mundo que conclui o ensino médio e quer ingressar no ensino superior nas universidades do nosso país. A solução encontrada foi fazer um processo seletivo, que é o vestibular e o Enem, para escolher quem entra e quem não entra. Porém, esse processo seletivo acabava por excluir muitas pessoas devido às dificuldades, aos acessos, às condições socioeconômicas que muitas pessoas enfrentam no cotidiano. E a política afirmativa busca trazer uma certa equidade para que as pessoas possam, sim, ter esse acesso à universidade", explica a pesquisadora.

Raissa Pequeno, estudante cotista do curso de Administração Pública da Uenf — Foto: Isadora Nogueira

Na Uenf, auxílios evitam evasão e encurtam distâncias

Em Campos dos Goytacazes, no Norte Fluminense, a implementação das cotas na Uenf foi decisiva para a democratização do ensino superior. Entre a entrada na universidade e a conquista do diploma, porém, há uma caminhada que exige um suporte para que o estudante não abandone a sala de aula em busca de emprego imediato.

É o caso de Raissa Pequeno, estudante cotista do curso de Administração Pública da Uenf. Moradora de São João da Barra, município vizinho, quase adiou o sonho da graduação por falta de recursos financeiros, mas encontrou nas bolsas da universidade a viabilidade para estudar e morar perto do campus.

"Me apaixonei pelas matérias e decidi que era isso que eu queria fazer. Eu quase fui trabalhar porque eu precisava de dinheiro e eu ia adiar para um ano a minha graduação. E quando eu descobri que a Uenf tinha bolsas e que eu receberia mais estudando do que no Jovem Aprendiz, eu sabia que era esse o meu destino e que não fazia sentido continuar adiando uma coisa que eu queria tanto, já que aqui eu conseguiria fazer as duas coisas e seria muito melhor para o meu futuro. Eu sou de São João da Barra, então o deslocamento para cá era muito difícil e com os auxílios que recebi no segundo ano de graduação eu consegui finalmente me mudar para frente da universidade. Então o deslocamento que eu fazia em uma hora e meia agora eu chego em cinco minutos na universidade, justamente devido aos auxílios que eu recebo", relata Raissa.

Na Uerj, o impacto dos 25 anos da lei pode ser medido em números. Um levantamento realizado pela própria instituição analisou os dados de ingresso e conclusão da graduação entre 2003 e 2025. Ao todo, 13.905 estudantes cotistas ingressaram na universidade nesse período; desse total, 45,4% já se formaram.

O estudo também desmonta argumentos contrários à reserva de vagas: nos cursos classificados como de alto prestígio, a nota média dos estudantes cotistas chegou a 5,25 (numa escala de zero a dez), superando a média dos alunos da ampla concorrência, que ficou em 5,08.

Para Vinícius Hozana, doutor em Educação pela Universidade Federal do Estado do Rio de Janeiro (Unirio), os números comprovam a eficácia da política quando acompanhada de estrutura adequada.

"Esse resultado contraria a ideia de que cotistas teriam rendimento inferior e por isso diminuiriam a qualidade do ensino na universidade. A ideia da análise não é evidenciar uma superioridade dos estudantes cotistas, mas demonstrar que, com políticas de acesso e manutenção desses estudantes na universidade, seu desempenho acadêmico é digno de nota", afirma Hozana.

Na prática, essa manutenção acadêmica transforma a rotina de alunos como Bryan Pinheiro, estudante cotista de Educação Física da Uerj. Primeiro de sua família a ingressar em uma universidade pública, concilia a graduação com atividades remuneradas dentro e fora do campus, viabilizadas pela política de assistência estudantil.

"Faço um projeto de pesquisa aqui dentro, um projeto de extensão também aqui dentro e dou aula num projeto social lá no Morro dos Prazeres, de futebol, para a rapaziada de lá. Hoje, basicamente, a maioria da minha renda vem de dentro da Uerj, né? Porque o aluno é cotista assim que ele ingressa. Ele tem direito ao auxílio permanência durante toda a graduação e ele consegue ainda fazer estágio aqui dentro", conta Bryan.

Além do suporte financeiro, o estudante destaca a importância da representatividade no ambiente acadêmico para o bem-estar e a permanência dos alunos negros.

"Quando você chega em um local e você vê pessoas parecidas com você, você se sente mais seguro, você se sente mais à vontade para ser você mesmo. Você não precisa ficar se podando, você não precisa ficar pensando em como você tem que agir, em como você tem que falar, em como você tem que se vestir para ver se você vai ser aceito ou não, porque vai ter pessoas como você", diz.

Na Uerj, o impacto dos 25 anos da lei pode ser medido em números. — Foto: Isadora Nogueira

O desafio da permanência e o combate ao racismo institucional

Embora os dados apontem avanços, o doutor em Educação Vinícius Hozana ressalta que o poder público precisa ir além da abertura das portas da universidade.

"Para a entrada na universidade, é importante fomentar bolsas de alimentação, transporte, moradia e apoio pedagógico e psicológico. E conforme a perspectiva antirracista, é fundamental enfrentar o racismo institucional e reconhecer os saberes e as trajetórias desses estudantes", pontua o especialista.

Ao olhar para a própria trajetória, Bryan Pinheiro resume o significado histórico da conquista iniciada há 25 anos no Rio de Janeiro:

"Eu sou o primeiro da minha família a pisar em uma universidade pública. Às vezes, essa pode ser a oportunidade mais preciosa que a gente tem, sabe?"

articles.title: Temporal provoca alagamentos e derruba árvore em carro em Sinop | G1
articles.standfirst: Chuva forte provocou alagamentos em diferentes pontos do município; árvore atingiu veículo ocupado por advogada e os dois filhos, mas ninguém ficou ferido.
articles.summary: O temporal com chuvas em Sinop registrou mais de 100 mm e causou alagamentos, além da queda de uma árvore sobre o carro de uma advogada e seus dois filhos.
articles.body:
Adicione o g1 como Fonte Preferida no Google

As fortes chuvas que atingiram Sinop nesta quinta-feira (26) provocaram alagamentos em diferentes pontos da cidade, deixando ruas e avenidas inundadas e dificultando o tráfego de veículos. Em meio ao temporal, uma árvore caiu sobre um carro ocupado pela advogada Jéssica Machado e seus dois filhos, no bairro Jardim Botânico . Apesar do susto, ninguém ficou ferido .

Segundo Jéssica, ela levava os filhos para a escola quando decidiu mudar o trajeto para evitar um trecho alagado da avenida Tarumã. Ao passar pelo bairro Jardim Botânico, percebeu duas motocicletas paradas em uma esquina e reduziu a velocidade para observar as condições da via. Pouco depois, a árvore caiu sobre o veículo.

“Eu resolvi não passar pela Tarumã, que tinha um acúmulo de água muito grande, e resolvi cortar caminho por aqui. Parei, vi uma movimentação na esquina de duas motos e fiquei olhando. Aí resolvi ir um pouquinho mais para frente. Foi nesse momento que caiu a árvore em cima de nós”, relatou.

Árvore caiu sobre carro durante temporal no bairro Jardim Botânico, em Sinop — Foto: Rhenzo Nogueira/TVCA

Com o impacto, as portas do veículo ficaram bloqueadas, e a família precisou sair pela janela, com a ajuda de pessoas que estavam nas proximidades.

“Minha primeira reação foi tentar ver se realmente meus filhos estavam bem. Graças a Deus, eles estão bem e não se machucaram”, disse.

Segundo a Secretaria de Meio Ambiente (Sema), a situação da árvore já estava sem sustenção e chuva forte contribuiu com a queda. A secretaria informou ainda que não havia chamado para essa árvore antes do temporal e que monitora outros pontos semelhantes.

Os pluviômetros registraram volumes entre 100 e 135 milímetros de chuva em quase duas horas . Diante das condições climáticas, a Defesa Civil emitiu um alerta à população sobre os riscos de chuvas intensas e ventos fortes.

Ao g1 , o Corpo de Bombeiros informou que havia registrado um chamado relacionado a alagamento. Um entregador pediu ajuda após ficar preso em um trecho inundado, mas conseguiu sair sozinho depois que o nível da água baixou, sem necessidade de atendimento da equipe.

Imagens registradas durante o temporal mostram ruas tomadas pela água, carros com água na altura das portas, motocicletas caídas e comerciantes retirando objetos de dentro dos estabelecimentos para evitar prejuízos (assista acima) .

O temporal também provocou vazamentos no Fórum de Sinop. Um deles atingiu o quadro geral de energia, localizado na sala da Central de Administração, gerando risco de curto-circuito. Por causa da situação, o expediente forense foi suspenso nesta quinta-feira.

Segundo a Prefeitura de Sinop, equipes da Secretaria de Obras estão nas ruas para avaliar os pontos atingidos pela chuva. Até a última atualização desta reportagem, não houve registro de feridos.

Durante períodos de chuva intensa, a orientação é evitar situações de risco e procurar abrigo seguro. A Defesa Civil recomenda que a população fique atenta aos alertas meteorológicos e evite transitar por áreas alagadas.

Não atravesse ruas alagadas a pé, de moto ou de carro.

Evite ficar próximo de árvores, postes, placas e estruturas metálicas durante ventos fortes.

Não procure abrigo embaixo de árvores durante tempestades com raios.

Evite contato com fios elétricos caídos e não se aproxime de áreas com risco de desabamento.

Se a água começar a invadir a residência, desligue a energia elétrica, se for seguro fazê-lo, e procure um local protegido.

Em situações de risco durante tempestades, a população pode acionar a Defesa Civil (199), o Corpo de Bombeiros (193) e o Samu (192).

articles.title: Deputadas da Alepe sofrem ameaças de morte e ataques racistas | G1
articles.standfirst: Mensagem cita nominalmente cinco parlamentares mulheres da Casa e tem conteúdo misógino e violento. Deputada Dani Portela registrou boletim de ocorrência e pediu apuração à presidência da casa.
articles.summary: Deputadas da Alepe sofrem ameaças de morte e ataques racistas em e-mail que detalha planos de sequestro e uso de explosivos contra parlamentares em Pernambuco.
articles.body:
Cinco mulheres, de diferentes etnias e idades, falam em microfones em um ambiente formal. A primeira mulher à esquerda tem cabelo cacheado escuro e uma flor vermelha. A segunda usa óculos e tem cabelo castanho liso. A terceira tem cabelo vermelho vibrante e maquiagem marcante. A quarta tem cabelo cacheado escuro e brincos grandes. A quinta mulher tem cabelo castanho claro e veste uma blusa estampada.

Adicione o g1 como Fonte Preferida no Google

Cinco deputadas estaduais de Pernambuco foram alvo de ameaças de morte em um e-mail enviado ao endereço institucional da deputada Dani Portela ( PT ), na quarta-feira (25). A mensagem, com conteúdo misógino e racista, cita nominalmente as parlamentares e afirma que elas seriam sequestradas e mantidas reféns em um ataque à Assembleia Legislativa de Pernambuco (Alepe).

As deputadas mencionadas são Dani Portela, Débora Almeida ( PSD ), Gleide Ângelo ( PP ), Rosa Amorim (PT) e Simone Santana ( PSB ). No texto, o autor também faz ofensas racistas direcionadas especificamente a Dani e Rosa.

A ameaça foi comunicada à presidência da Alepe e à Superintendência de Inteligência (Suint) da Assembleia. O caso foi denunciado pela deputada Dani Portela, que também registrou um boletim de ocorrência para que o caso seja apurado.

No e-mail, o autor diz possuir um revólver e dinamite e ameaça entrar armado na Alepe, onde faria as deputadas reféns. Além da invasão à assembleia, o autor ameaça atacar as residências das cinco deputadas caso o plano seja impedido.

Em nota, a deputada Dani Portela afirmou que já recebeu ameaças semelhantes anteriormente e relacionou o episódio à violência política de gênero e raça, que, segundo ela, atinge especialmente mulheres negras que ocupam cargos públicos.

Em 2022, quando era vereadora do Recife, Dani Portela denunciou ter sido vítima de injúria, calúnia, difamação e ameaças de morte por causa da publicação de uma notícia falsa em sites e redes sociais.

A postagem afirmava que a parlamentar queria substituir o busto do general Humberto Castelo Branco, primeiro presidente do Brasil após o golpe militar de 1964 e apontado como um dos responsáveis por crimes na ditadura , pela imagem de Fidel Castro, ex-presidente de Cuba e um dos responsáveis pela Revolução Cubana.

No ano seguinte, Rosa Amorim recebeu um e-mail com ameaças de teor machista e LGBTfóbico . Na mensagem, o autor propôs a criação de um "projeto de lei" para a realização de "estupros corretivos" como forma de "cura lésbica".

Até a publicação desta reportagem, somente Dani Portela havia se manifestado sobre as ameaças recentes.

Em comunicado enviado à imprensa, ela destacou que as ameaças representam uma violência contra a democracia e afirmou que o episódio não deve impedir a atuação das mulheres na política. Ela citou o assassinato da vereadora Marielle Franco (PSOL-RJ), em 2018, e as ameaças sofridas por outras parlamentares negras e LGBTQIA+.

O g1 questionou a Alepe e a Polícia Civil sobre medidas adotadas com relação às ameaças, mas não obteve respostas até a última atualização desta reportagem.

articles.title: Defesa Civil de BH emite alerta de risco geológico após temporal | G1
articles.standfirst: Aviso vale para as regiões Oeste e Centro-Sul até segunda-feira (30). Em cinco horas, volume de chuva ultrapassou 50 mm em parte da capital.
articles.summary: A Defesa Civil de BH alerta para risco de deslizamento de terra e desabamentos nas regiões Oeste e Centro-Sul após temporal atingir 50 mm em apenas cinco horas.
articles.body:
Adicione o g1 como Fonte Preferida no Google

A Defesa Civil de Belo Horizonte emitiu, na noite desta quinta-feira (26), um alerta de risco geológico moderado para as regiões Oeste e Centro-Sul da capital. O aviso, válido até a próxima segunda (30), foi divulgado após os fortes volumes de chuva registrados nas últimas horas e diante da previsão de novos temporais .

Ao longo do dia, houve enxurradas e alagamentos em vários pontos da Grande BH. Em Contagem , por exemplo, uma cascata se formou na Rua Dr. Vicente Búfalo, na Vila São Paulo, onde uma obra do metrô está em execução ( veja vídeo acima e leia mais abaixo ).

Conforme a Defesa Civil de Belo Horizonte, até segunda-feira, há risco de deslizamentos de terra, quedas de muros e desabamentos devido ao encharcamento do solo. O órgão orienta que os moradores fiquem atentos a sinais como:

Caso algum desses sinais seja identificado, a recomendação é sair imediatamente do imóvel e acionar a Defesa Civil pelo telefone 199. Em situações de emergência, o Corpo de Bombeiros deve ser chamado pelo 193.

O órgão também recomenda evitar cortes em barrancos, não jogar lixo ou entulho em encostas, não despejar esgoto nesses locais e consertar vazamentos em caixas-d'água e reservatórios.

Entre 13h e 18h desta quinta, a região Oeste registrou o maior volume de precipitação da cidade, com 50,6 milímetros. Em seguida, aparecem Centro-Sul (44,8 mm), Noroeste (31,6 mm) e Barreiro (24,2 mm).

O acumulado de chuva até 26 de novembro já ultrapassou a média histórica do mês em nove das dez regiões de Belo Horizonte. A média climatológica é de 236 milímetros.

A Centro-Sul lidera o acumulado mensal, com 396,2 milímetros, o equivalente a 167,9% da média esperada para novembro. Na sequência, aparecem Pampulha (365 mm), Oeste (354,8 mm) e Noroeste (351,4 mm).

A única região que ainda não atingiu a média histórica é o Hipercentro, com 212,8 milímetros, ou 90,2% do volume esperado.

De acordo com a Defesa Civil, áreas de instabilidade continuam atuando na Região Metropolitana de Belo Horizonte, com previsão de chuva de diferentes intensidades nas próximas horas.

O temporal que atingiu Belo Horizonte e Região Metropolitana causou transtornos na tarde desta quinta-feira (26). Houve registro de alagamentos e outras ocorrências na capital mineira, em Contagem e em Ribeirão das Neves.

Por volta das 17h, a forte chuva provocou uma enchente na Rua Geraldo Vasconcelos, no bairro Estoril, e uma enxurrada na Rua Papoula Azul, no bairro Havaí, na Região Oeste de BH.

O Anel Rodoviário ficou alagado em alguns trechos, principalmente na altura do bairro Betânia. Vias do Barreiro também foram afetadas, e a Unidade de Pronto Atendimento (UPA) da região teve acúmulo de água.

Em Contagem, o temporal causou uma enxurrada na Rua Dr. Vicente Búfalo, na Vila São Paulo, onde há uma obra do metrô em execução. A água caiu em formato de cascata e invadiu a casa de uma moradora ( veja vídeo acima ).

"A Defesa Civil de Contagem informa que uma equipe já está na Vila São Paulo, na região Industrial, para avaliar a situação e definir as medidas necessárias diante das fortes chuvas que atingiram a região", disse a prefeitura.

Conforme a concessionária Metrô BH, a ocorrência está relacionada a um "problema preexistente no sistema de macrodrenagem da região" que interfere nas obras da linha 2. A concessionária disse que "tem contribuído com a elaboração de projetos para melhorar o escoamento da água da chuva".

Em Ribeirão das Neves, houve acúmulo de água na Rua Cataguases, no bairro Sevilha B.

Segundo o Corpo de Bombeiros, a corporação recebeu seis chamados para ocorrências envolvendo pessoas ilhadas na Grande BH ao longo do dia. No entanto, os militares não precisaram atuar, pois as enchentes escoaram.

Os moradores de Belo Horizonte podem acompanhar alertas sobre chuvas fortes, granizo, tempestades, vendavais, alagamentos e risco de deslizamentos de terra pelo canal público da Defesa Civil no WhatsApp.

Também é possível receber avisos por SMS. Para se cadastrar gratuitamente, basta enviar uma mensagem de texto com o CEP da rua para o número 40199. Em seguida, o usuário recebe uma confirmação.

Além disso, os alertas são divulgados pelos perfis oficiais da Defesa Civil nas redes sociais.

"A emissão de alertas regionalizados é uma das principais estratégias da Defesa Civil de Belo Horizonte para antecipar situações de risco e orientar a população sobre possíveis mudanças nas condições meteorológicas", diz a prefeitura.

Três imagens lado a lado mostram os impactos de uma enchente. À esquerda, uma rua alagada com carros submersos. Ao centro, uma grande cascata de água barrenta. À direita, o interior de um edifício com o chão coberto de água, onde um homem usa um rodo para limpar e outras pessoas observam.

articles.title: Escolas de Fortaleza vão fechar 1 hora mais cedo devido ao calor | G1
articles.standfirst: O fim do ano letivo também foi antecipado devido às altas temperaturas. Professores e alunos reclamaram do calor a diretores das unidades e também nas redes sociais.
articles.summary: O fim do ano letivo também foi antecipado devido às altas temperaturas. Professores e alunos reclamaram do calor a diretores das unidades e também nas redes sociais.
articles.body:
Adicione o g1 como Fonte Preferida no Google

As escolas da rede pública de Fortaleza vão encerrar as atividades uma hora mais cedo todos os dias devido ao aumento da temperatura causado pelo El Niño . A mudança deve começar em dezembro. A informação foi repassada pela Secretaria Municipal da Educação (SME) nesta quinta-feira (26).

Em nota, o órgão municipal disse que foi solicitado ao Conselho Municipal de Educação de Fortaleza a avaliação da redução de uma hora por turno nas escolas públicas em virtude das altas temperaturas registradas em toda a cidade. Professores e alunos reclamaram da situação a diretores das unidades e também nas redes sociais.

O que mudaria na prática? As escolas, pela manhã, funcionarão de 7h as 10h, encerrando as atividades com o fornecimento da merenda escolar. À tarde, o turno irá de 13h as 16h, também encerrando com a alimentação.

O g1 conversou com um professor de Fortaleza que não quis se identificar. Ele falou sobre o impacto do calor nas atividades escolares.

“Tem muito aluno e professor passando mal nas salas de aula. Muito quente, insuportável. Eu mesmo fui um que já passei mal dentro da sala de aula, para ter ideia do tamanho do calor que está fazendo”, disse o docente.

Outra mudança na educação de Fortaleza causada pelo El Niño é a antecipação do fim do ano letivo . A previsão era encerrar no dia 7 de janeiro de 2027, mas a data foi antecipada para 23 de dezembro.

“Aos sábados, estão sendo enviadas atividades domiciliares para os alunos para cumprir esses dias que seriam de janeiro", explicou o professor.

"Desde o começo de novembro, até dezembro, todos os sábados tem aula remota com atividades domiciliares que os professores enviam para os alunos através da coordenação das escolas e os alunos depois devolvem para os professores darem um visto, e registrar, para que não haja nenhum prejuízo para os estudantes”, complementou.

Ceará enfrenta onda de calor nos primeiros dias de janeiro de 2026 - Foto: Kid Júnior/SVM

A SME disse que já investiu cerca de R$ 14 milhões na aquisição de novos equipamentos e na realização de adaptações necessárias nos espaços escolares. O órgão disse que, no início da gestão, o cenário encontrado foi de apenas 72 unidades (14,3% da rede apta) climatizadas.

“A pasta trabalha para atingir a meta de climatizar 100% da rede municipal até o fim de 2028 e reforça que 471 escolas (92% da rede) já têm pelo menos uma sala de aula com ar-condicionado e, nos últimos dois anos (2025 e 2026), 192 instituições receberam aparelhos, totalizando 1.347 aparelhos instalados”, disse o órgão municipal.

A Prefeitura de Fortaleza instituiu um comitê de enfrentamento aos efeitos do El Niño. A medida foi publicada no Diário Oficial do Estado desta quarta-feira (25).

O novo grupo vai atuar como “instância intersetorial de articulação, planejamento, monitoramento e apoio à tomada de decisão, destinada a coordenar e integrar as ações do Município de Fortaleza para prevenção, mitigação, preparação, resposta e recuperação diante dos efeitos associados ao fenômeno El Niño”.

A finalidade, conforme a prefeitura, é promover a atuação integrada dos órgãos e entidades municipais na gestão dos riscos e desastres decorrentes das condições climáticas associadas ao fenômeno El Niño, especialmente aqueles capazes de afetar a população, os serviços públicos essenciais, a infraestrutura urbana, o meio ambiente e os recursos hídricos.

Entre as ações relacionadas ao comitê, a prefeitura listou situações que considerou como “Cenários de risco prioritários” . São elas:

Enxurradas, Inundações e Instabilidade de Encostas

Ventos Fortes, Raios e Danos à Infraestrutura

Calor Extremo, Baixa Umidade e Impactos na Saúde e Bem-Estar

Estiagem, Pressão Hídrica e Risco de Incêndios Urbanos e Florestais

Erosão Costeira, Ressacas e Avanço do Mar

Além dos pontos citados, a prefeitura também elencou como cenários de risco situações de "efeitos combinados", quando houver simultaneamente eventos extremos de mais de uma categoria.

Outra medida também é recomendar a suspensão de eventos públicos e privados com grandes concentrações de pessoas . “Ou a aplicação de medidas mitigatórias de riscos em eventos [...], fundamentando-se no monitoramento de tempo, clima e saúde, nos respectivos avisos e alertas, bem como nas diretrizes do Protocolo de Calor e Saúde e dos planos setoriais, independentemente da ocorrência de fenômenos climáticos, como o El Niño, ou de outros eventos adversos”, detalhou o documento.

articles.title: Brasileiros atraídos para lutar na Rússia sofrem golpe de recrutadores | G1
articles.standfirst: Recrutadores prometiam pagamentos de até US$ 100 mil e funções longe da linha de frente. Contudo, ao chegarem, eram enviados para o combate, mesmo sem treinamento.
articles.summary: Recrutadores prometiam pagamentos de até US$ 100 mil e funções longe da linha de frente. Contudo, ao chegarem, eram enviados para o combate, mesmo sem treinamento.
articles.body:
Adicione o g1 como Fonte Preferida no Google

Uma reportagem do jornal americano "The New York Times" publicada nesta quinta-feira (26) relata que dezenas de brasileiros foram atraídos por recrutadores também brasileiros para se juntarem ao Exército russo, com a promessa de pagamento de US$ 50 mil (cerca de R$ 287 mil) a US$ 100 mil (R$ 574 mil).

A proposta indicava que eles assumiriam funções longe da linha de frente — por exemplo em cozinhas ou no conserto de armas. No entanto, ao chegarem à Rússia , eles foram enviados diretamente para o front da guerra da Ucrânia , mesmo com pouquíssimo treinamento.

Além disso, os brasileiros recrutados tiveram seus pagamentos roubados pelos intermediários .

Segundo o jornal, eles foram induzidos a assinar documentos em um idioma que não entendiam. Os papéis davam aos recrutadores controle sobre as contas bancárias e salários dos brasileiros.

Exército russo — Foto: Alexander Zemlianichenko/AFP

A reportagem foi baseada nos relatos de nove recrutas brasileiros e de familiares de outros três, além de documentos analisados pelo NYT. O jornal teve acesso a fotos, vídeos, mensagens de áudio e texto, procurações, contratos militares e extratos bancários.

A prática de recrutar estrangeiros para lutar como mercenários no front tem sido empregada tanto pela Rússia quanto pela Ucrânia durante a guerra , que está prestes a completar cinco anos e sem perspectiva de ser finalizada. Recrutas de outras nacionalidades também relatam ter sofrido golpes similares na Rússia, recrutados para lutar com promessas de altos salários em empregos longe da linha de frente.

Segundo o NYT, o recrutamento ocorria por meio de vídeos nas redes sociais Instagram, TikTok e YouTube e incluía promessas de salários de milhares de dólares. A maioria dos vídeos terminava com o direcionamento para o Telegram , plataforma de mensagens de origem russa que é frequentemente utilizada para esquemas criminosos.

Ao chegar à Rússia, os brasileiros eram recebidos pelos recrutadores, que fizeram a tradução na hora da assinatura dos documentos, segundo o NYT. Fernando Mazzo, de 45 anos, disse ao jornal que eles só perceberam que haviam caído em um golpe quando já estavam alistados no Exército russo e estavam recebendo treinamento em uma instalação militar nos arredores de Moscou.

Eles descobriram o golpe ao suspeitar de transações feitas em suas contas bancárias e comparar entre si suas contas em aplicativos de telefone.

Uma das vítimas do golpe, Igor Pereira Santos, de 37 anos, afirmou ao jornal que foi enviado para a linha de frente poucas semanas após chegar a Moscou.

O brasileiro também relatou que os US$ 25 mil (cerca de R$ 143,5 mil) que havia recebido por se juntar ao Exército russo desapareceram de sua conta. Durante uma missão na Ucrânia, Igor ficou gravemente ferido nas duas pernas após ser atingido por estilhaços.

Um outro brasileiro, Anderson de Oliveira Ferreira, de 24 anos, foi à Rússia com o sonho de comprar uma casa e um carro elétrico com o dinheiro que ganharia. Ele mentiu à família dizendo que foi trabalhar como segurança.

articles.title: Número de pedidos para primeira CNH cresce 193% em 2026, segundo Ministério dos Transportes | G1
articles.standfirst: Também foram emitidas 2,7 milhões de CNHs, alta de 16,8% na comparação com os primeiros 11 meses do ano passado.
articles.summary: Também foram emitidas 2,7 milhões de CNHs, alta de 16,8% na comparação com os primeiros 11 meses do ano passado.
articles.body:
Autoescola, instrutor autônomo, motorista, CNH, Carteira Nacional de Habilitação, dirigir, Detran, Detran-SP — Foto: Reprodução/EPTV

Adicione o g1 como Fonte Preferida no Google

Até novembro deste ano, foram abertos 8,59 milhões de processos para obtenção da primeira Carteira Nacional de Habilitação (CNH) no país, segundo o Ministério dos Transportes .

O número representa um aumento de 193,3% em relação ao mesmo período de 2025, quando foram registrados 2,93 milhões de pedidos.

No mesmo período, foram emitidas 2,7 milhões de CNHs, alta de 16,8% na comparação com os primeiros 11 meses do ano passado.

Segundo a pasta, a diferença entre o número de processos abertos e o de carteiras emitidas se explica pelas etapas exigidas para a obtenção do documento.

Os requerimentos contabilizam os candidatos que iniciaram o processo de primeira habilitação, enquanto as emissões consideram aqueles que concluíram todas as fases e receberam a CNH.

O resultado é explicado pela entrada em vigor das novas regras para obtenção da CNH, aprovadas no fim do ano passado. A principal mudança foi o fim da obrigatoriedade de realizar aulas em autoescolas.

Com as alterações, os cursos teórico e prático podem ser feitos fora das autoescolas, em instituições credenciadas ou com instrutores autônomos autorizados. Esses profissionais são responsáveis por registrar e validar a presença e a participação dos candidatos nas aulas.

As mudanças, no entanto, não extinguiram as autoescolas nem os cursos oferecidos por elas. Os candidatos que preferirem podem continuar seguindo o modelo tradicional, com toda a formação teórica e prática realizada em uma autoescola.

articles.title: Why old ammunition can become a ticking time bomb: The science behind controlled explosions
articles.summary: The US military has described as a “huge success” the controlled detonation of nearly five tonnes of lead azide, a highly volatile explosive compound, at
articles.body: The US military has described as a “huge success” the controlled detonation of nearly five tonnes of lead azide, a highly volatile explosive compound, at an ammunition plant in Iowa. The operation had raised concerns over potential health and environmental hazards, with residents in the surrounding areas expressing fears over the impact of the blast. The US Army subsequently issued an “all clear” for the area around the ammunition plant, saying the risk had been reduced to “as close to zero as is absolutely humanly possible”.The explosives had remained in storage for nearly 20 years and had deteriorated through a process known as recrystallisation. This made the lead azide increasingly sensitive to friction, movement and other disturbances, raising the risk of an accidental explosion. The compound was considered particularly dangerous because of the possibility of it detonating without an external trigger.What is a controlled explosionA controlled detonation is the deliberate triggering of an explosive device or material by trained and authorised personnel, either to neutralise a threat or to dispose of explosives safely. Bomb disposal teams, military engineers and explosive ordnance disposal (EOD) specialists usually carry it out after assessing the nature and condition of the explosive and the risks involved. The aim is to ensure the blast happens at a designated place under controlled conditions, so that people, property and nearby infrastructure are not endangered. It differs from an accidental explosion, which happens without control, and from a controlled implosion, which is used to bring down buildings.Unexploded ordnance (UXO) is among the most common reasons for such operations. Bombs, shells, mortar rounds and grenades that failed to go off when fired or dropped can lie buried for decades and turn dangerous when disturbed by construction, farming or excavation. The method is also used for ageing or unserviceable ammunition held by the armed forces and for improvised explosive devices recovered by security agencies. At times, the material is first moved to a secure range before it is destroyed.India has seen several such operations. In March 2021, the Army's Southern Command carried out Operation Thiruvallur at Gummidipoondi in Tamil Nadu, where nearly 10 tonnes of unexploded ordnance had piled up at a scrap yard. In August 2024, Army personnel and Tripura Police destroyed 27 mortar bombs from the 1971 war, found while a pond was being dug at Dulal Nama village. In July 2024, Indian Air Force personnel from Kalaikunda blew up a World War II bomb found during field excavation at Bhulanpur in West Bengal after the area was evacuated. In October 2025, an Army EOD team from Panagarh dealt with a suspected World War II mortar shell recovered from the Ajay river in Birbhum.The technique has also been used on unsafe material from industrial and civilian sites. During Operation Visphotak Mukt Bandargah in 2021, specialists from the Central Ammunition Depot at Pulgaon helped dispose of explosive material recovered in Mumbai and elsewhere. Reports said over eight lakh kg of unidentified explosive objects, with more than 2,000 kg of RDX or TNT equivalent, had been handled in Mumbai.The term is sometimes used for planned demolitions too. The Supertech twin towers in Noida were brought down on August 28, 2022, using nearly 3,700 kg of explosives, and four apartment complexes in Maradu, Kochi, were demolished in January 2020 for violating coastal regulations. Strictly speaking, these are controlled implosions. Controlled blasting in mining, tunnelling and road building is a related field, where bodies such as CSIR-Central Institute of Mining and Fuel Research work to limit vibrations, noise and flying debris.The Army is now looking for safer ways to dispose of old ammunition. A 2026 Army Design Bureau problem statement proposed a containerised demolition system that could contain the effects of small-scale disposal inside ammunition depots, reducing the need to transport explosives. Detonation is not always the answer, however. In June this year, the navy safely extracted an unexploded missile warhead lodged in a fuel tank of the tanker MT Olympic Life.

articles.title: Andy Burnham joined by former PMs for Widdecombe service
articles.summary: Hundreds of guests attended including Andy Burnham, David Cameron, Liz Truss and Boris Johnson.
articles.body:
Andy Burnham was joined by former prime ministers as he attended a memorial service for the late politician Ann Widdecombe.

Hundreds gathered for the Service of Remembrance at Westminster Cathedral on Thursday afternoon, including David Cameron, Liz Truss, Boris Johnson and Rishi Sunak.

Home Secretary Shabana Mahmood, Reform UK leader Nigel Farage and deputy leader Richard Tice, along with former Conservative Chancellor Philip Hammond and Speaker of the House of Commons Sir Lindsay Hoyle, were also in attendance.

Bishop James Curry, the Auxiliary Bishop of Westminster, led the service after the Archbishop of Westminster, Richard Moth, was taken to hospital earlier.

Moth, who is the head of the Catholic Church in England and Wales, underwent tests after he "felt unwell", Westminster Diocese said.

During the memorial, tributes were paid by Widdecombe's nephew, Reverend Roger Widdecombe, and independent crossbencher Lord Alton of Liverpool.

Widdecombe's nephew said his aunt's death was "a tragedy," but added the service was to "pay tribute to Aunt Ann" and "celebrate and thank God for a life well lived".

He said: "Words such as integrity, brave, kind, delightful, indefatigable, interested, tireless, fun, all express something of the amazing woman that Ann was."

He noted his aunt was "certainly a lot of fun," recalling family anecdotes which prompted guests to laugh.

Finishing the eulogy, he said: "We loved her very much, and we'll miss her."

The service, which lasted about 70 minutes, featured a motet, a psalm and two hymns sung by the Westminster Cathedral choir.

The prime minister was later seen leaving the cathedral with former prime ministers Rishi Sunak and Boris Johnson.

Widdecombe, a former Conservative minister and Reform UK's justice spokeswoman, was found dead at her home in Haytor, on Dartmoor, Devon, on 9 July, aged 78.

Joshua Kerry, 28, of Byrley Road, Rotherham, South Yorkshire, was charged with her murder.

A trial before a High Court judge is scheduled for 8 June, and a plea and case management hearing on 29 January.

Widdecombe's family announced plans for a public memorial service following her death.

The late politician served as Conservative MP for Maidstone and the Weald in Kent for 23 years and was appointed to ministerial roles in Sir John Major's government in the 1990s.

She became a member of Reform in 2019 as a party spokeswoman.

Away from politics, she appeared on the BBC's Strictly Come Dancing in 2010 and was a runner-up on Celebrity Big Brother eight years later.

In the 1990s she converted to Catholicism, a move she later described as the best decision she ever made.

articles.title: Chief medical officer Gregor Smith resigns on mental health grounds
articles.summary: Sir Gregor Smith said he was unable to continue with the "exceptional challenges" his role demands.
articles.body:
Scotland's chief medical officer, Sir Gregor Smith, has resigned on mental health grounds.

The 55-year-old, who has served in the position since December 2020, has faced questions over his role in the handling of avoidable deaths at NHS Grampian in recent weeks.

Smith said in a statement that he did not "currently enjoy the good mental health necessary" to continue in the job, adding that guiding the country through the Covid pandemic and its aftermath had "taken its toll".

First minister John Swinney thanked Smith for his service, adding that he had led the country through "one of the most demanding periods the Scottish health service has faced."

Dame Anna Dominiczak has been named as interim chief medical officer following Smith's resignation.

Did Scotland's departing chief medical officer actually do anything wrong?

John Swinney insists medical chief was not told to go amid growing NHS Grampian scandal

A question of trust in the NHS could be Swinney's most dangerous political moment

Smith's resignation comes after a surgeon, Dr Mohammed Habib, called for NHS Grampian to face a corporate homicide probe .

Habib leaked an unpublished review, carried out in 2022, which found 19 avoidable deaths among 45 patients in liver and pancreatic surgery at Aberdeen Royal Infirmary (ARI).

Smith and former health secretary Humza Yousaf were aware of issues at the time.

Health secretary Angela Constance has since commissioned an independent review into hepatobiliary surgery at the health board.

An oversight team has also been appointed following a separate report by Healthcare Improvement Scotland (HIS) , which found "major deficiencies" in NHS Grampian's leadership and culture.

Smith said: "It has been a privilege to be the CMO of Scotland for the last six-and-a-half years, but it has become very clear to me that the nature and purpose of the role is not generally understood.

"Like many colleagues across the health system, those years of the pandemic and afterwards have taken their toll.

"Events over the last few days have shown me that I don't currently enjoy the good mental health necessary to continue with the exceptional challenges that this role can expose you to."

He added: "No-one in public life is unaccountable. I am confident, however, that the review initiated by the cabinet secretary will show that I provided my advice in relation to Grampian hepatobiliary service consistent with the role of the chief medical officer."

Dominiczak was appointed as the Scottish government's chief health scientist in July 2022 and is regius professor of medicine at the University of Glasgow.

The Scottish government described her as a "world-leading cardiovascular scientist and clinical academic".

Constance said: "Dame Anna has played a key role in driving medical innovation in her time as chief scientist and she brings a wealth of clinical experience to the role of interim chief medical officer.

"I know she will be keen to work collaboratively with health and care staff across the country as we continue to ensure people are able to access the right care in the right place."

Smith spent 15 years as a GP in Larkhall before becoming medical director for primary care at the NHS Lanarkshire health board.

He became a senior medical officer within the Scottish government in 2012 and was appointed deputy chief medical officer three years later.

Smith was appointed interim chief medical officer in April 2020 after predecessor Catherine Calderwood resigned over the flouting of Covid regulations.

His appointment was made permanent in December of that year after becoming a familiar face appearing alongside Yousaf and then first minister, Nicola Sturgeon, at televised daily Covid briefings.

He was awarded a knighthood for his services to public health and the NHS in 2022.

Swinney said he "recognised and respected" Smith's decision to step down.

"Gregor became interim chief medical officer at the beginning of one of the most demanding periods the Scottish health service has faced," he said.

"He provided crucial senior clinical advice to government throughout the pandemic and then through the difficult recovery period that followed.

"I would like to thank him for his service to Scotland during Covid and beyond."

Health Secretary Angela Constance said: "In addition to his work during Covid, Gregor has been a strong advocate for person-centred healthcare, prevention and action to reduce health inequalities, drawing throughout on his experience as a practising GP.

"I thank Gregor for his commitment to public service and for his dedicated contribution to public health in Scotland."

BBC Scotland News became aware of new allegations from NHS Grampian on Wednesday.

Claimes published in The Times newspaper alleged a surgeon at Dr Gray's hospital in Elgin, Moray, attempted to take over a knee operation while he was recovering from a medical procedure and under the influence of drugs.

It also detailed a separate incident in which a surgeon had a physical altercation with a registrar who it is claimed suggested they were about to replace the wrong hip of a patient who was lying unconscious on the operating table.

The HIS report, published on 12 November, outlined serious shortcomings in management and leadership at NHS Grampian.

HIS medical director, Dr Simon Watson, described the report as "the most serious review" the healthcare watchdog had ever written, calling its findings "unprecedented".

Constance announced the independent review on Saturday. She said there was no "cover up" surrounding the 2022 report, adding that the review would be "100% transparent".

A spokesperson for Yousaf said he would answer questions about what he was briefed on and his follow-up actions at the upcoming independent review.

Reform UK's health spokeswoman, Helen McDade, said she expected "other resignations".

She added: "Gregor Smith clearly did not want to share information beyond the fact that he knew about the 2022 report, he appeared to be hiding things, but he may well be being a made a scapegoat."

articles.title: Falklands War veteran say UK government ministers are hiding behind GDPR on Sir Galahad bombing files
articles.summary: Falklands veterans demand UK government release more files from 1982 inquiry.
articles.body:
A Falklands War veteran who was left severely burned in an attack on his ship has accused ministers of hiding behind data protection in refusing to release all files on the bombing.

The undefended supply ship Sir Galahad was hit by Argentinian planes in June 1982m killing 48 people, including 32 Welsh Guards.

The Welsh Guards had previously been blamed for not leaving the ship earlier, but files released later cleared them of any blame .

Simon Weston said veterans "just want to know who is responsible for making terrible decisions".

The UK government said it had to strike a balance between respecting legal obligations and giving veterans the answers they needed.

A 1982 Royal Navy inquiry was held in private and its findings unreleased.

Excerpts have been released over time, including in 2024, when two files were released.

But five files comprising 308 witness statements are closed and, under the terms of the Public Records Act 1958, are not due to be released until 2065.

More than 100 were injured in the bombing. Another eight died on the Sir Tristram while dozens of others were injured.

Weston, and fellow veteran Mike Hermanis, attended a Commons debate on the management and disclosure of records from the inquiry on Wednesday.

'We're not interested in anything but the truth'

Weston, 65, a former Welsh guardsman, said he was "disappointed" by the response.

He said ministers must "stop hiding behind GDPR", referring to the regulations that have governed data protection since the 2010s.

"It wasn't meant for what went on in '82 and statements that were made in '82. So we feel that people will be hiding behind a law that wasn't theirs to hide behind," he said.

"We're not interested in anything other than the truth. We just want to know who is responsible for making terrible decisions."

The scheduled release date was too late to help anyone, he said.

"We'll all be dead by then and it benefits not us or the families.

"It's been a terrible tortuous 44 years and some of the families have passed away since then, sisters and brothers of the bereaved, and it's just not fair on them."

Hermanis, 64, from Newport, was on board the ship as a 19-year-old guardsman.

He said ministers' refusal to unseal files until 2065 was "very deflating".

"After being there for 90 minutes and at the 11th hour, that was a sledgehammer blow to us.

"But we've been campaigning for 44 years, so we'll just keep on going, keep knocking, somebody's going to open our door."

He said watching the debate had been "overwhelming" and he was moved to tears by the amount of support from backbench MPs.

"These MPs, they're all different parties, and they came together to give us truth, justice and transparency. That's all we want: honesty."

Labour's Newport East MP, Dame Jessica Morden, secured the debate after being contacted about the issue by Hermanis, who is her constituent.

Morden also said ministers had confirmed to her that some of the transcripts and tape recordings of key witnesses given as part of an inquiry into the bombing were "missing from the record, having somehow been lost at an unknown point over the years".

"It is really hard to see, 40 years later, how the current approach can be justified," she told MPs.

The former Conservative leader Iain Duncan Smith, who served in the Scots Guards, said it was "shameful" the Welsh Guards had been blamed when those above them had made mistakes.

Chris Evans, the Labour MP for Caerphilly, said he was "utterly disgusted" the Welsh Guards had been blamed for the tragedy, and said the UK government had a "chance to put that right".

The minister for the armed forces, Louise Sandher-Jones, said she wanted to be clear the Welsh Guards were not at fault.

"The Welsh Guards were absolutely not to blame in any way. In fact, as we have heard, they showed amazing bravery and heroism with their actions that day," she told MPs.

But she said ministers had legal obligations they must respect.

"Section 40 of the Freedom of Information Act protects the personal information of living individuals. That is why those files currently should remain closed until 2065. There are also obligations under the Data Protection Act 2018," she told MPs.

Sandher-Jones also said it was important to consider carefully "whether the wider impact of releasing reports to do with a historical event means that, in some future tragedy, we constrain being able to get to the truth".

articles.title: Why is Italy angry with Ukraine for striking Russian ships off Libya?
articles.summary: Analysts say Rome fears instability in Libya could hurt its energy interests and efforts to curb irregular migration.
articles.body:
Italy has denounced Ukraine for carrying out attacks against Russian vessels in Libyan waters, saying it was wrong to “violate Libya’s sovereignty”.

Rome’s rebuke marks a crack in its relationship with Ukraine, which Italy has largely supported since Russia’s full-scale invasion in 2022, including with military assistance.

It coincides with growing concern about the involvement of foreign powers in a divided Libya, as well as the risk of other nations being drawn into the Russia-Ukraine conflict.

So why has Italy weighed in now, and what makes Libya so strategically important to Rome?

Why did Ukraine carry out an attack in Libyan waters?

Kyiv claimed it sank a Russian warship and struck a cargo vessel transporting military equipment off Libya’s coast on Sunday night. The attack on the warship at Benghazi port in eastern Libya killed two naval officers of the self-styled Libyan National Army (LNA), according to Libya’s eastern-based forces.

Ukraine’s Foreign Minister Andrii Sybiha described the vessels as legitimate targets, arguing Kyiv had the legal right to defend itself against “Russian aggression”.

He stressed that Ukraine’s actions were “not intended to harm Libya or its people” and that Kyiv respects Libya’s territorial integrity.

“Ukraine is not ‘dragging’ anyone into the war or ‘transferring’ the war anywhere,” Sybiha said in a statement on Telegram.

Musa al-Koni, the vice president of Libya’s Tripoli-based Presidential Council, called the attack “a declaration of war against the Libyan state”.

Libyan authorities “hold the Ukrainian side fully responsible for these terrorist acts”, he added.

The LNA, a rival power that controls eastern and southern parts of Libya and maintains close relations with Russia, promised to retaliate against the Ukrainian attack “at the appropriate time and place, and by the appropriate means”.

Libya is divided between the UN-recognised government in Tripoli and a parallel administration based in Benghazi, backed by the LNA and its renegade commander, Khalifa Haftar.

Italy’s Foreign Minister ⁠⁠Antonio Tajani said it was a mistake for Ukraine to “violate Libya’s sovereignty” and that Rome, which has a small military presence in Libya, had received no prior notice of the operation.

“Italy was absolutely unaware of Kyiv’s intentions to strike in Libyan territorial waters, even inside a port,” Tajani told Italy’s Corriere della Sera newspaper.

Italy’s far-right League party, which is a member of the coalition government, also criticised the attack, saying it risked sowing instability inside Libya.

The comments expose a rare rift with Ukraine, which Italy has largely supported in the war against Russia. Italy has provided Ukraine with more than 3 billion euros ($3.29bn) worth of military aid, according to data from the Kiel Institute think tank, while also backing sweeping sanctions against Russia.

However, there has been division within Italy’s government over further aid to Ukraine, with Deputy Prime Minister Matteo Salvini, who heads the League party, opposing more weapons shipments or funding.

Matteo Villa, a senior research fellow at the Italian Institute for International Political Studies (ISPI), told Al Jazeera that Ukraine’s recent attack off Libya is likely to deepen these domestic tensions.

It “gives Salvini an opportunity to strengthen his case, questioning whether Western military assistance risks enabling Ukraine to pursue objectives that run counter to Italy’s own national interests”, said Villa.

What relationship does Italy have with Libya?

Italy, whose southern islands lie 300km (186 miles) across the Mediterranean from the Libyan coast, has spent years building ties with rival factions in western and eastern Libya.

“Over the past few years, Rome has shifted from almost complete support for the UN-backed Western government in Libya towards building working relationships with the Haftar-controlled East as well,” said Villa.

Italy has also for years helped provide funding, equipment and training for Libya’s maritime authorities, despite reports of migrants being abused and tortured in Libyan custody.

The aim has been to curb irregular migration from Libya to Italy, one of the most perilous and contested Europe-bound routes .

Alessia Melcangi, a nonresident senior fellow with the North Africa Program at the Atlantic Council’s Rafik Hariri Center and Middle East Programs, said Italy’s condemnation of Ukraine partly serves as a form of “damage control” to help Rome balance its competing geopolitical interests.

“Rome needs to demonstrate that its relationships with Kyiv, Tripoli and Benghazi give it meaningful influence over developments affecting its security,” Melcangi told Al Jazeera. “Otherwise, perceptions of exclusion or ambiguity could cause lasting diplomatic damage.”

Why is Italy concerned about conflict spilling into Libya?

Villa said Rome’s concerns are fuelled by its geographical proximity to Libya, as well as its economic and strategic interests there, specifically in terms of energy and “migration control”.

“Last year, Libya accounted for roughly a quarter of Italy’s crude oil imports, making it its largest supplier, and the country is by far the main departure point for migrants reaching Italy by sea,” said Villa.

Aldo Liga, a research fellow at the Middle East and North Africa Centre at ISPI, told Al Jazeera that potential escalation that further destabilises Libya would “threaten the security of trade routes and energy flows”, creating a volatile security situation in the Strait of Sicily.

“Instability in Libya is perceived as a direct threat to Italy’s national interests,” he said.

In his interview with Corriere della Sera, Foreign Minister Tajani cited the presence of the Italian military and Italian petroleum company Eni in Libya as being among his concerns about the Ukrainian intervention.

“What happened is worrying,” Tajani said, referring to the Ukrainian attack. “The war between Russia and Ukraine must be prevented from widening, avoiding new outbreaks from occurring.”

articles.title: Iowa residents mark Thanksgiving with lingering fears after chemical detonation
articles.summary: The U.S. Army blew up the nation’s entire stockpile of lead azide, a chemical used to make explosives, saying the first checks show Wednesday’s controlled detonation in Iowa didn’t spread toxic dust to nearby homes and farms.
articles.body: A day after the Army detonated its stockpile of the toxic compound lead azide at an Iowa munitions plant, hundreds of federal workers returned to the scene Thursday for additional testing as local residents sought to ease any lingering fears with Thanksgiving Day festivities. More than 300 employees and contractors with the Environmental Protection Agency began collecting over 1,000 samples from the air, land and water, pulled from homes, schools, farms, drinking water supplies and elsewhere, said agency Administrator Lee Zeldin in a social media post. They intended to finish the job by the end of the day and “transparently provide all results as they come in from our laboratory” within one to two days, he added. The announcement of ongoing testing was welcomed by residents of the small farming community of Middletown, where the 68 drums of lead azide, once used to make bombs, had been stored at the Iowa Army Ammunition Plant before the Army made a calculated decision to detonate the volatile compound, triggering environmental concerns and voluntary evacuations around the blast site in southeastern Iowa. Following Wednesday’s controlled detonation of the material, the Army said the measure appeared a success — its initial findings indicated the plume of dust hadn’t reached nearby farms and residences and EPA monitoring had detected no lead in the air. Tim Thomann, who was preparing to host 15 relatives at his home in Middletown for Thanksgiving, watched as the nearby command center remained a “beehive of activity,” with workers canvassing the area to take soil samples. “The Army said it looks like a success,” said Thomann, as he planned a holiday feast of turkey, ham and homemade ice cream. “I just hope they can continue testing so we have that peace of mind.” Instead of thinking about Thanksgiving preparations earlier this week, Blaine Dial, another Middletown resident who lives near the munitions plant, was, like many other residents, sealing windows and doors as a precaution from effects of the blast. Dial said Thursday that environmental monitoring remains “absolutely key” after learning about how lead azide, a heavy metal, can be particularly dangerous to children and pregnant women. “We never really know with the way the wind was blowing, where anything may have landed,” Dial told NBC News. Since the military announced, and then delayed, plans for the detonation over the past two weeks, residents and environmental groups have voiced concerns about potential health and environmental impacts and about a lack of information about what to expect. The Army said the safest option had been detonating the stockpile right away because it was degrading and might explode on its own at any time as the weather got colder. Maj. Gen. Eric Shirley, who led the Army operation, said the risk was “reduced as close to zero as it’s absolutely humanly possible.” “As we saw in the immediate aftermath through overhead coverage, all the lead azide barrels were definitively removed,” Shirley said Wednesday following the detonation. “There was no secondary explosion, there was no kickout, there was no infrastructure damage in or around our installation.” To prepare for the detonation, earthen barriers were put up and foam and water were poured onto a pair of bunkers holding the 5 tons of lead azide. Officials said those measures appear to have absorbed much of the blast. An alert sent to cellphones late Wednesday afternoon said it was safe to resume normal activities. The Federal Emergency Management Agency also issued an all-clear around the plant, the military reported. President Donald Trump posted on social media that the Army did a “great job,” while acting Army Secretary Adam Telle, along with the Republican governors of Iowa and Missouri, also said it appeared to be a success and that the explosion was well-contained. The EPA’s air quality data was promising, said Andrew Whelton, an environmental engineering professor at Purdue University who has helped communities recover from chemical disasters. Yet he stressed that samples need to be tested in a lab to determine whether people face health risks. “This should take days to weeks,” Whelton said. “But what we may see is different guidance issued to different communities based on how far they are from the detonation area and whether or not they were upwind or downwind.” Colin Wellenkamp, the executive director of the Mississippi River Cities and Towns Initiative, said water treatment facilities along the Mississippi and Missouri rivers will be testing periodically to make sure that there are no detectable spikes. The stockpile was brought to Iowa from bases around the country in 2009, according to Robert Cekada, director of the Bureau of Alcohol, Tobacco, Firearms and Explosives. The lead azide was stored just in case the military needed to use it again. Questions remain over why the Army had allowed the lead azide to deteriorate over the years to the degree that it required a controlled detonation, which carried a risk to properties and the environment. The materials “should never have been allowed to degrade to this point,” Josh Turek, Iowa’s Democratic senator-elect, said in a Facebook post. Kevin and Linda Ross, who own a home and pottery business in Wever, about a mile from the plant, said they were personally testing for lead after worrying their garden and fish pond may get contaminated. Ten initial tests from around their home came back negative, they said Thursday. They had been so busy safeguarding their home, including wrapping their chicken enclosure in plastic, that they already decided to postpone their family’s Thanksgiving celebration to Friday. “It was just going to be too crazy, and we’re just going next door to our daughters,” Linda Ross said, “but it worked out for the family, and that’s fine.” The Army scheduled the detonation for Wednesday because the winds were blowing to the southwest and away from populated areas including Burlington, a city of just under 25,000 people along the Mississippi River. Government officials had encouraged residents closest to the site and in range of the plume to evacuate, and others to stay indoors. Schools not already closed around the Thanksgiving holiday canceled classes and many businesses closed. Matt Mitchell, a truck driver from Middletown, said he witnessed Wednesday’s blast, expecting something noticeably spectacular, but instead of a loud boom or major plume of debris, it was no different than other testing he might hear from the nearby plant, he said. Still, as he was traveling to the Wisconsin border for Thanksgiving, he said he was grateful for two things: the continued testing and his community’s return to the peace and quiet that was upended after the days of national attention. “Honestly,” Mitchell said, “I can’t wait for social media to calm down again.”

articles.title: US judge blocks Trump’s FCC attempt to target Disney’s ABC stations
articles.summary: The judge said the FCC chair has taken US President Donald Trump’s rhetoric ‌‌as his ‘marching orders’.
articles.body:
A United States judge has barred the Federal Communications Commission (FCC) from putting the licences of eight Walt Disney-owned ABC TV stations up for early review, a blow ⁠⁠to President Donald Trump’s efforts to rein in US media companies.

US District Judge Loren AliKhan, in Washington, DC, granted Disney’s request for a preliminary injunction on Wednesday. The injunction barred the FCC from holding a hearing on the licences, a step that could have led to their revocation and forced the stations off ⁠⁠the air.

“This is not a close case,” AliKhan wrote, saying the FCC appeared to be carrying out a retaliatory campaign, driven by Trump, that threatened the broadcaster’s free-speech rights.

AliKhan, who was nominated by former President Joe Biden, said ABC had detailed “a campaign of retaliation against them in response to their exercise of their First Amendment rights,” which on its own is an ‘irreparable injury’”.

FCC Chair Brendan Carr, whom Trump named to the position in January 2025, “has taken President Trump’s rhetoric as his marching orders”, the judge added.

A spokesperson for ABC News said, “Today’s decision is an important victory for ⁠⁠the First Amendment.”

Carr ordered reviews of licences ‌for the eight stations in April, a day after Trump urged ABC to fire late-night host Jimmy Kimmel, even though the renewals were not due to be considered until October 2028 at the earliest. The FCC had not ordered an early review in more than 50 years before April.

Disney and ABC sued the FCC in August to block the early review of the stations in Los Angeles, Chicago, New York and other cities, arguing that the Trump administration was trying to punish the network over broadcast content in violation of the US Constitution.

In response to AliKhan’s decision, an FCC spokesperson has said that the granting of the injunction was “wrong on the facts and ⁠⁠wrong on the law — as controlling Supreme Court precedent makes clear.”

They added, “We will continue to use our lawful ⁠⁠authority to hold broadcasters accountable to their public interest obligations.”

Trump has repeatedly urged broadcasters to drop comedy or news programmes that he dislikes or that have been critical of him or his administration.

Broadcast stations need FCC licences to use public airwaves. While licence revocations are extremely rare, critics said that the risk of losing a licence could have a ⁠⁠chilling effect on a broadcaster and raise concerns about government interference.

Trump has waged aggressive ⁠⁠attacks on the news media, and the latest move follows a two-year-long battle between Trump and Disney.

In July, Trump repeated a call for ABC stations to lose their licences because the network refused to air a prime-time speech he gave that said US elections are vulnerable to fraud.

In reacting to the judicial decision, Democratic FCC Commissioner Anna Gomez said the ruling “brings ‌‌badly needed accountability to a commission and an administration that have politicised the machinery of government in a sustained campaign of censorship and control”.

The FCC is also investigating ABC daytime talk show “The View,” which discusses US politics, after saying it may be subject to federal rules requiring broadcasters ‌‌to ‌‌provide equal-time opportunities to political candidates.

Disney previously said that as a result of that investigation, the programme did not invite any political candidates to appear before the November midterm elections, and the broadcaster cited the FCC’s “pressure campaign”.

articles.title: Qatari, Egyptian leaders discuss Gaza ‘ceasefire’ and regional security
articles.summary: Sheikh Tamim bin Hamad Al Thani is in Cairo for an official visit aimed at further strengthening bilateral relations.
articles.body:
Qatari Emir Sheikh Tamim bin Hamad Al Thani and Egyptian President Abdel Fattah el-Sisi have discussed regional tensions and efforts to implement the Gaza “ceasefire” during talks in Cairo.

El-Sisi received the emir on Thursday at Cairo International Airport upon his arrival for an official visit at the Egyptian president’s invitation. After a reception at the presidential palace, the talks began.

Sheikh Tamim’s visit was aimed at further strengthening bilateral relations across various sectors, including investment and energy, as well as coordinating diplomatic efforts to de-escalate tensions and bolster regional security, Qatar said.

“Today, I discussed with my brother, President Abdel Fattah el-Sisi, the latest developments in the region and the importance of continuing consultations and coordinating joint efforts to address current challenges, in a way that helps safeguard our region’s security and stability and fulfil its peoples’ aspirations for peace and prosperity,” Sheikh Tamim said on X after the meeting.

The two leaders discussed efforts to promote regional stability, Egyptian presidential spokesman Mohamed el-Shenawy said in a statement.

They stressed the importance of “intensifying regional and international efforts to prioritise political solutions and dialogue and prevent tensions from widening”, warning of “serious consequences for regional and international security and stability”, the statement added.

The talks also addressed developments in Palestine with el-Sisi outlining Egypt’s efforts to implement the Gaza “ceasefire”.

The Egyptian leader emphasised the need for all parties to uphold the agreement, ensure the delivery of humanitarian aid to the Gaza Strip and begin recovery and reconstruction programmes without delay.

Qatar’s Emiri Diwan said in a statement that the two leaders exchanged views on the latest regional and international developments, “particularly the situation in the Gaza Strip and joint mediation efforts to solidify the ceasefire”.

The Egyptian statement said el-Sisi also reaffirmed Egypt’s “full support for the security of Qatar and other Gulf states”, stressing that “the security of the Gulf is an integral part of Egypt’s national security”.

It also said the two leaders discussed ways to strengthen economic ties and cooperation in areas of mutual interest and they agreed to continue “intensifying political consultations and coordination”.

The meeting was also attended by Qatari Prime Minister and Foreign Minister Sheikh Mohammed bin Abdulrahman bin Jassim Al Thani and other senior officials from both countries.

articles.title: 'AI is great but it can't deliver a lamb', say agriculture students
articles.summary: Agricultural colleges in East Yorkshire and Lincolnshire say they have seen a rise in applicants.
articles.body:
Students looking to forge careers in agriculture believe there is still a need for hands-on skills as they embrace artificial intelligence (AI).

Bishop Burton College, in East Yorkshire, and Riseholme College, in Lincolnshire, which specialise in land-based subjects, said they had seen a rise in the number of pupils enrolling on some of their courses.

Students have been learning how they can use AI in the industry while also understanding the value of traditional methods.

Katy Cranston, who studies agriculture, land management and livestock production at Bishop Burton, said: "I can see why people are worried about AI. I think it's a great tool, but AI can't deliver a lamb, can it?"

Cranston added: "I'm learning what is needed to succeed in my career choice and I can see how technology assists farming, but I also know where its limits are.

"AI won't be impacting farming as quickly as some other careers, so I can see why parents and people my age are reconsidering their career choices and perhaps looking at agriculture."

Sharon Kirby, programme leader for agriculture degree courses at Riseholme, said: "There are some roles that AI can't do yet, but my goodness, it can give them a lot of background data to allow us to make informed decisions thereafter.

"I think the future is quite exciting around AI and technology.

"It's just enhancing it and capturing how best it can work for us without having a detriment to the labour market."

AI has been useful for many farmers across England, with some using it to grow crops indoors without sun and soil , or to spot issues with cattle .

But Kirby said, while AI can assist farming and agriculture, vocational courses in the sector teach students things that AI cannot do, such as preparing a sheep for the Lincolnshire Show.

"AI can't wash a sheep, can't trim a sheep up, can't handle a sheep, can't encourage it to walk in the right manner, to stand up in the right manner," Kirby said.

"I think hands-on courses are still the way forward. AI is about enhancing what we're doing and helping us to work smarter."

Beth Curtis, vice principal at the two sites, said courses such as agriculture, animal management, equine studies and health and social care had all seen increasing numbers of students choosing them.

The East Yorkshire college said 46% of 2,000 secondary school children it surveyed said AI had made them consider pursuing a more hands-on career.

It also found 77% of 2,000 parents were concerned about the impact of AI on their child's future job prospects.

The findings come after Prime Minister Andy Burnham announced schools would offer technical subjects with courses linked to local industries and designed to give children a clearer pathway into work.

Curtis added: "We're not against AI. We embrace new technology and recognise how important it is to the world.

"However, there are certain skills that we teach here at the colleges that won't ever be able to be replaced by AI."

Louis Horstwood, who studies agriculture, land management and crop and plant production, thinks more people are drawn to the agricultural industry because it is more "reliable" and less impacted by AI.

"AI can't change the points on a plough," she said.

"It might let you know there is a problem with them, but if the subsoil breaks them and you're out in a field, it won't be AI fixing it, it will be me.

"I don't see farming being taken over by AI any time soon."
